methodological_questions: What is the operational definition of offensive reorganization and of the baseline L?
Does within-spell reorganization relative to L predict the change in PPP after team, opponent and game-state adjustment?
Is the sample (148 spells, n=986) large enough for a stated MDE rho, and what is the unit of analysis?
Can the association be separated from team-quality and pace confounds using placebo absences?

historical_evidence.finding: Running play type X raising the same team's next 1-5 possession PPP showed flat global lifts (SPOT_UP lag-1 +0.027), which disappeared after team-season demeaning; within-team memory was essentially none except SPOT_UP lag-1.
Decaying cross-possession memory gate failed: DRIVE lifts were flat (+0.015 to +0.021) and collapsed within team; team-quality confound noted; verdict failed_gate.

HasConn share vs pace: beta -0.86 (p=0.0266) but within-team-season correlation -0.002 (p=0.782); play-type mix shifts (CUT +1.353, SPOT_UP -1.248) were clearer than efficiency; no stint clock, so poss/48 was period-implied.
Connector presence on star shielding and lineup PPP was null (HasConn on-off PPP mean -0.041, p=0.939, n=73); TO rose with connectors (wrong sign); lineup ORtg lift was a talent confound.
Process-only state persistence did not clear the rolling-window overlap null: excess -0.010, cluster-bootstrap 95% CI [-0.012,-0.009], N=1,060,893 possessions; mechanical floor noted as a risk.
Sequence-memory horizon of about 2-3 possessions: per-lag AUC rose from 0.5621 to 0.5911 with gain almost entirely at lag-1; absolute AUC only about 0.591; time-split test 2025-26.
Player-level BEST vs AVOID PPP gap +0.427 in the same direction as the team gap, but only 3 players cleared n>=30 in both tiers.
Routing to best player: A5 vs A3 shrank from +0.94 to +0.03 pts/100 on 520 matchups; adequately powered null on model-scored outcomes.
Star suppression by lineup and forced play type reported large PPP gaps (e.g., Giannis PULL_UP 0.848 vs DRIVE gap -0.540) with no placebo or matching; later work treated similar gaps as artifacts.
Descriptive BEST/AVOID tier tendencies by team and player; player samples 10-178 possessions; no outcome test.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Lag-based play-type memory on next-possession PPP, read from global horizons
failed_approaches.why: Flat non-decaying global lifts were produced by team-season confounding and vanished after within-team demeaning (recorded as C_artifact).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Decay-sanity gate for play-type cross-possession memory
failed_approaches.why: Lifts were flat across lags and collapsed under within-team baseline; team-quality confound (recorded as C_artifact, failed_gate).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Connector presence as a driver of star shielding and lineup PPP
failed_approaches.why: Null PPP effect with adequate power in the record (B_powered_null); lineup lift attributed to talent confound (p=0.51 after TALENT adjustment).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Latent process-state persistence above a window-overlap null
failed_approaches.why: Excess was negative with CI entirely below zero; mechanical floor and sample-size risks recorded (B_powered_null).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Star-initiator suppression by lineup and forced play type
failed_approaches.why: No placebo or matching; mechanism unclear (E_unclear); large gaps in small cells (n=30-59).

evidence_establishes: Within this project, team-level and within-team comparisons of play-type or lineup effects on PPP have repeatedly shrunk toward zero or been flagged as artifacts once team quality is controlled.
Sample sizes for player-level or cell-level PPP comparisons are often far below what is needed (only 3 players reached n>=30 in both tiers in FAM:SF-APPS-036).
Cross-possession sequence effects in the existing data are small (AUC about 0.591 in FAM:SF-APPS-059), so a reorganization effect of any size would need careful isolation.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record studies offensive reorganization relative to a baseline L as a predictor of change in PPP; the exact question has not been answered.
No record defines L or the reorganization measure used here, so none can be reused as a validated instrument.
No record reports an MDE rho or a power calculation for a spell-level design with 148 spells.
No record tests player absence spells as the unit, so spell-level effects and their placebo behaviour are unknown.
Retrieved records do not show whether the 2025-26 partial data changed any earlier results.
own_inferences: The question as posed has at least three undefined components (reorganization, L, rho), so it cannot be tested as written.
Using change in PPP from pre-absence to post-absence raises a regression-to-the-mean and selection risk, because absences are chosen by injuries and rotations that correlate with team quality.
The 148 spells and n=986 units likely differ in unit; if the test is at spell level, n=148 may be too small for modest effects given the small effects seen elsewhere in this project.
uncertainties: The meaning of 'L' (baseline lineup, last game, or a league-level reference) is not given.
It is unclear whether n=986 refers to possessions, games or player-team units, and how it relates to 148 spells.
The MDE rho is recorded without a value or definition.
Whether 2025-26 playoff and regular-season partial data are included is not stated.
Retrieval returned records only at the family level; full methods for SF-APPS-092 and SF-APPS-087 were cut and not read.

historical_effect.explanation: Prior records show that PPP-based effects in this project frequently collapse under team-quality and within-team baselines, and that unplaced sample sizes produce unreliable cells. That history moved the decision from a plain test to do_not_proceed until L, reorganization and the spell design are pre-specified with placebo and within-team controls.

blocking_constraints.text: Offensive reorganization and baseline L are undefined; without a fixed operational definition the predictor cannot be measured reproducibly.
148 spells with an unspecified MDE rho is likely underpowered for modest PPP effects, as seen in FAM:SF-APPS-036 and FAM:SF-APPS-087.
Absences correlate with team quality and rotation, and prior work shows team-quality confounds produce artifacts (FAM:SF-CHT-029, FAM:SF-APPS-073).

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record answers the exact question of reorganization relative to L predicting change in PPP. Adjacent records cover pace and play-type mix shifts (FAM:SF-APPS-092), connector effects on PPP (FAM:SF-APPS-087), play-type memory artifacts (FAM:SF-APPS-073, FAM:SF-CHT-029), and short sequence horizons (FAM:SF-APPS-059). These support caution about confounding and power but do not estimate the target effect.

risks.text: Reorganization and L are not defined; any measure built on play-type or initiator labels inherits labelling noise.
Play-type and possession labels are derived from play-by-play in a graph database; their validity for reorganization is unverified.
Team quality, opponent, minutes, score margin and pace could drive both reorganization and PPP change (see FAM:SF-CHT-029, FAM:SF-APPS-087).
148 spells and an unstated MDE rho may not support detection of realistic effects (see FAM:SF-APPS-036, FAM:SF-APPS-069).
Change in PPP measured using possessions after the absence can leak post-period information into the predictor if L is defined using future games.
Star-level gaps without placebo controls were treated as artifacts (FAM:SF-CHT-009); a placebo-absence design is required.
Overlap or mechanical structure in possession sequences can produce apparent persistence (FAM:SF-APPS-069).
Many play types, lags and tiers have been examined in this project; without pre-specification, a post hoc primary effect is likely.
Pooling 2022-23 to 2025-26 and partial 2025-26 data may mix rule and roster changes; playoffs differ from regular season.
Spell-level exposure may be thin for specific play types or absences, making reorganization estimates noisy.

design.estimand: Not yet estimable. Minimum viable estimand: within-spell association between a pre-registered reorganization index (change in play-type/initiator distribution relative to a pre-registered baseline L) and the change in team PPP across the absence, after team-season and opponent adjustment.
design.unit: Player absence spell (one row per spell), with possession-level PPP aggregated within pre-absence and absence windows; the unit must match the n=986 count, which is unclear.
design.sample: 148 spells as recorded, restricted to regular season 2022-23 to 2024-25 and completed 2025-26 regular season (from 2026-04-13); 2025-26 playoffs only after 2026-06-21; partial data excluded. Report any exclusions.
design.power: Compute an MDE for rho under the pre-registered spell design before analysis; if the MDE exceeds effects seen in prior project records (about 0.01-0.03 PPP in FAM:SF-APPS-073 and FAM:SF-APPS-069), report the design as underpowered and do not interpret a null as evidence of no effect.
design.controls: Team-season fixed effects; within-team demeaning; opponent strength; starter and lineup composition; minutes and possession count; score margin and pace; playoffs indicator. Predictor and outcome windows strictly separated to prevent lookahead.
design.falsification: Placebo absences from non-absence stretches of the same players and teams; pre-absence reorganization predicting pre-absence PPP trend; a negative-control play-type outcome not expected to respond.
design.multiplicity: One primary estimand and one primary baseline L pre-registered; all other play types, lags and tiers labelled exploratory with Holm correction if reported.
design.decision_rule: Proceed to a primary claim only if the primary estimate with spell-clustered CI excludes zero, survives placebo absences and within-team demeaning, and the design MDE is below the effect of interest. Otherwise report as null or inconclusive.
design.data_version: Pinned data snapshot with stated date of 2026-11-01; 2025-26 regular season used only after 2026-04-13 and playoffs only after 2026-06-21; record all partial-data exclusions and the exact definition of n=986 and of L.

methodological_questions: Does offensive reorganization relative to a baseline L predict change in points per possession?
How should reorganization be measured from play-by-play and derived play-type possession records?
What sample size and exposure are needed for spell-level analysis (n=148 spells, minimum detectable effect rho)?
How should confounding by player quality, opponent and game context be handled?
args.query: Prior project studies of player absence and offensive reorganization, measuring change in points per possession relative to a baseline L, using NBA play-by-play, substitution intervals and derived play-type possession records across 2022-23 to 2025-26 seasons.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
How much the offense reorganizes (relative to L) predicts the change in points per possession.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=986; n=148, mde rho; 148 spells

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
